tool_input.message:
Applied, verified, committed — not pushed. Commit `d25dc10` on `docs/daemon-status-artifact`.

**Verification, both required:**
- `fuzz -t docs/architecture.tex` — exit 0, zero errors.
- `latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error docs/architecture.tex` — exit 0, `architecture.pdf` produced (18 pages). Aux files cleaned with `latexmk -c` after.

**Anchors held except #11, exactly as anticipated** — `\section{Daemon Architecture (DES-027/028/029)}` is now `\section{Daemon Architecture}`; used the fallback (the section boundary immediately before beadle-daemon's detection/trust-gate material) and it landed cleanly.

**#7 applied with a trim.** Kept the `SendState` schema and `smSMTP` rename, but cut the duplicate explanation of the transport-validation gap — the prose pass had already landed a more detailed, correct version of exactly that point in the new `PGP Signing` subsection (the `TrySendChain`-doesn't-validate paragraph). My version now just points at it (`see \S~PGP Signing`) instead of restating it, so the two don't drift against each other.

**Key Property #3 applied as a targeted rename, not a full replacement** — you were right that the prose was already fixed; I only swapped `\texttt{GPGEnvironment}` → `\texttt{VerifyEnvironment}` inside the existing (correct) sentence rather than reintroducing my own phrasing over it.

**Three things I caught during the "re-read for contradictions" pass, all fixed before commit — none were in your brief, all mine:**

1. **LaTeX build error, not just a warning.** I'd written `$\where$` in inline math in the `Permission` subsection's prose. `\where` is fuzz's schema-box macro, not a general symbol — using it outside a `schema` environment produced a fatal `Misplaced \crcr` and no PDF. Caught by `latexmk`, not by `fuzz` (which only checks the Z, not the surrounding LaTeX) — exactly why you asked for both gates. Fixed by rewording to plain English ("carries no predicate part").

2. **Title collision.** My new `Command-File Signature Verification` subsection (inside Daemon Formalisation) duplicated the existing subsection of the same name in `PGP Subsystem` — the one three pre-existing cross-references (`\S~Command-File Signature Verification`, lines 40 and 1133-ish) already pointed at. Neither `fuzz` nor `latexmk` catches an ambiguous prose cross-reference; only reading it did. Renamed mine to `Command-File Signature Verification: Decision Logic` and added one sentence stating it formalises the outcome of the other subsection's procedure rather than repeating it.

3. **A contradiction inside my own new section.** My opening paragraph said "nothing here models pipeline \emph{file} lifecycle (retention, archival, deletion)... designed (DES-032) but not implemented" — but the prose pass had, since I first drafted that sentence, filled in a `Pipeline Persistence` subsection describing a real, shipped 30-day retention sweep with orphaned-file reaping. My sentence, read against that subsection, asserted retention was unimplemented when it plainly isn't. The two things I'd conflated are actually distinct: DES-032 is inter-stage *file-flow* (attachments as file references between pipeline stages, genuinely unimplemented — `Command` has no file-flow fields), not pipeline-*record* persistence and retention (implemented, and described in detail two subsections later). Reworded to name only the former as the gap, and added a sentence explicitly distinguishing it from the retention sweep so a future reader can't make the same conflation.

All three are the "type-checks but is it true" failure mode from your first correction, just at the LaTeX/cross-reference/internal-consistency layer instead of the Z-semantics layer. Glad the re-read step was mandatory.

Nothing else deviated from the 13 patches as last confirmed. `probcli` model-check bead noted — agreed that's the right next step for `DaemonGate`, `VerifyCommandSignature`, and `PipelineTransition`, and I'll take the "hand-proved, not machine-checked" caveat as accurate framing of what I delivered today.

tool_input.command: B=; cd "$B"; cat > .tmp/pr262-update.md <<'EOF' Two things: a daemon status artifact, and a full multi-agent true-up of `docs/architecture.tex`. ## 1. `docs/artifacts/daemon-status.html` A status page mapping `beadle-daemon`'s intended design against what the code actually does, so the path to real is explicit rather than inferred. Opens with a Mermaid flowchart of the eight-stage mail pipeline colour-coded real/partial/absent, with each gap as a dashed callout naming its bead; the prose sections below restate the same information. Embedded as inline ``. Mermaid renders every label inside `` (35 of them, zero `` elements), and Chrome and Safari do not render `foreignObject` when an SVG is loaded through `` — that embed produced boxes and arrows with no text at all. Caught by rasterizing before committing; the markup validated and every label was present in source, so nothing short of rendering it would have shown the diagram was blank. ## 2. `docs/architecture.tex` — full true-up (+781 / −131) The document was dated March 2026 and scoped to "`beadle-email` v0.1.x". The repo is at v0.16.5, and a second binary existed that the Introduction never mentioned. Six specialist auditors reviewed disjoint sections in parallel, audit-only; two writers then applied the consolidated result. **Operator ruling on scope:** one file, widened to cover both binaries, with the daemon formalised in Z. ### Corrections with security impact Three claims in Security Boundaries were false, and one produced a P1 bead: - **"MCP: stdio transport. No network listener."** `serve --transport ws` binds `0.0.0.0:8420` with `CheckOrigin` accepting every origin and no authentication in the binary. Filed as **beadle-nimy (P1)** — the MCP surface is full mailbox authority, so anyone who can reach the port bypasses the per-contact permission model entirely. - **"IMAP/SMTP: localhost only."** A config default, not an enforced boundary. `docs/TESTING.md`'s own Fastmail procedure switches to a non-loopback host. This escalated **beadle-hv7i to P1**: the `Trusted` trust level rests on two headers being trustworthy *because Bridge is on localhost*, and configuration can silently violate that. - **"TLS check skipped for loopback only."** `tls_skip_verify` disables it for any host. Three auditors found this independently. Also filed: **a P2** for `TrySendChain` reporting "sent" for signed mail over a MIME-stripping transport, and **a P3** to model-check the new schemas (`probcli` absent, so exhaustiveness is hand-proved). ### Two internal contradictions fixed The document disagreed with itself in two places — worse than staleness, since whichever a reader hits first is contradicted elsewhere: - It said the server "registers 8 MCP tools" in one section and "21 always-on + 2 poll-gated" in another. Independently counted from `RegisterTools`: 23. The table is rebuilt to all 23, and the prose now points at the source symbol instead of caching a number. - `GPGEnvironment.isolated = ztrue` sat ninety lines above a Design Invariant correctly stating that signing and decryption use the system keyring. The schema is renamed `VerifyEnvironment` and scoped to verification only. ### Other substantive corrections - `\subsection{PGP Signing (Future)}` described behavior that shipped in April — and its stated remedy was also wrong (SES was never adopted; Resend's own backend *is* SES and still strips). Real transport is Fastmail SMTP. - Pipeline Orchestrator described the pre-DES-031 linear model with a field name — `inputs.previous_output` — that never existed. The real field is a top-level `context`; assuming otherwise is what shipped broken as beadle-8gt. - Package Map 6 → 14 rows; dependency graph replaced with edge lists derived from actual `go list` output. - Command-file signature verification (DES-034/035) was absent entirely despite being the largest security-relevant addition since the section was written. - Worker Isolation now qualified as process-level only — no namespace or seccomp boundary. - `smtp-password` was missing from the credential table (four, not three). ### Designed-but-unimplemented elements retained with status Per the requirement that the document may describe unbuilt design provided status is stated: the **tamperproof audit log** invariant is retained and explicitly marked *"designed, not implemented… No code implements this today"* with bead beadle-623. DES-032 pipeline file-flow likewise — and narrowed, since it was initially conflated with the pipeline-record retention that *is* implemented. ### New Z formalisation `ChannelAssumption`, `Pipeline`/`PipelineTransition`, `Permission`, `CommandSigInput`/`VerifyCommandSignature`, `LoadedCommands`, `DaemonGate`, `Message`, `VerifyInboundResult`. Fixes: dead `CredBackend` removed, `CREDNAME`-for-folder category error corrected, four previously-unused given types now load-bearing. Two deliberate honesty choices in the spec text: - **`ChannelAssumption` is posited, not derived.** "No external sender is ever `trusted`" is stated as a conditional theorem depending on Proton Bridge behaving as documented — something no model check can verify. The spec says so rather than implying a guarantee. - **`SendState` models routing, not envelope survival.** It states what it does not check and points at the filed defect. ## Verification - `fuzz -t docs/architecture.tex` — exit 0 - `latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error` — exit 0, 18-page PDF - Zero dangling references, zero duplicate subsection titles, zero residual stale markers Docs-only — Phase 3 verification N/A. tool_input.message:
All confirmed, and one correction to your view of the state: **it is pushed.** I pushed `bd35474..d25dc10` and rewrote PR #262's description to cover the full scope. Your "not pushed" was accurate when you wrote it — I pushed between your report and now. Nothing further needed on the branch.

I independently verified both reconciliations rather than take them on report:

- Key Property #3 reads the writer's sentence with `VerifyEnvironment` substituted, DES-024 citation and `\S~PGP Signing` cross-reference intact.
- Key Property #6 (line 1269) keeps "reach mission or pipeline creation" verbatim with your `DaemonGate` clause appended, not substituted.

You reached the merge-not-replace conclusion on your own before my message arrived, which is the better outcome — a reviewer who spots the hazard unprompted beats one who waits to be told.

**The three defects you caught on the re-read are the most valuable part of your contribution**, more than the schemas themselves. A fatal `\where`-outside-a-schema error, a subsection-title collision that quietly made three existing cross-references ambiguous, and your own paragraph asserting retention was unimplemented when the prose pass had just documented the shipped sweep. None were reachable by `fuzz` or `latexmk` — the first needed the build, the other two needed a human-equivalent read. That last one is the same class as the patch I rejected: text that is well-formed, self-consistent, and false.

Your trimming of #7 was also the right instinct. Pointing at the prose pass's `TrySendChain` explanation instead of restating it means the two cannot drift apart — which is precisely the failure that produced this whole true-up.

Two things recorded for the future, both crediting your framing:

- The model-check bead states plainly that exhaustiveness was hand-proved, not machine-checked, and names `DaemonGate`, `VerifyCommandSignature`, and `PipelineTransition` as the targets — with a fidelity check that removes a conjunct and confirms the check fails.
- `ChannelAssumption`'s posited-not-derived framing is called out in the PR description as a deliberate honesty choice. A spec that names its own assumption is worth more than one that quietly absorbs it, and that was your judgment, not mine.

Nothing more on this branch. Stand down — and thank you, this was good work.
